answer: A farm faking 447 aliases needs 447 separate verifiable records of this kind, each checked against the issuing authority, so the cost multiplies per alias instead of staying flat. Signalman service record works as the check: shifts worked in one signal box across years of trains. The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. The pulse record shows the asymmetry: scale multiplies the cost but never the reward, the quartz entry is checkable by anyone, and the karst window closes before a farm can catch up.
